relevance_note: A pediatric liver-disease WES cohort that gives individual-level detail (diagnosis, treatment, outcome, Group A) for one TNFAIP3 carrier: "One patient with Familial Behçet-Like Autoinflammatory Syndrome caused by a TNFAIP3 mutation received infliximab treatment".
method_note: Read the full paper by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script in the scratch directory, no table transcription. Scope: of the 80 cohort children (216 enrolled, 136 excluded), only the single TNFAIP3 carrier is in scope; no relatives are described. Labelled 'unnamed person 1' (rule 6: cohort paper, no own label). No variant description is printed in the text; the paper refers to Supplementary Table 1, which is not in the file, so the variant row has variant_original_string 'not reported'. Zygosity, inheritance and the authors' P/LP-vs-VUS class for this variant are not stated in the text (the 46 'genetic results' include 7 VUS carriers), so they are 'not reported'; 'caused by a TNFAIP3 mutation' is the authors' causal attribution only. Parental testing: the methods say WES was done in patients and their parents, but the VUS paragraph says parental samples were not always available, and nothing is stated for this patient; recorded as 'not reported' in the variant row (the methods sentence is used only as diagnosis basis). Cohort-wide statements applied to this person because they explicitly cover all patients: 'No consanguineous marriages were found in the cohort' (consanguinity no), 'All patients survived during the follow-up' (alive), 'in a Chinese pediatric population' (ethnicity; cohort-level, from a single Shandong hospital). Liver enzyme elevation is recorded as observed from the patient's explicit placement in Group A (abstract) plus the individual statement that transaminases normalized after infliximab. Not recorded: absence of cholestasis implied by Group A assignment rules, and autoimmune hepatitis or infections from the study's exclusion criteria (v3 study-criteria rule); all 20 checklist items are 'not reported'. Contradictions/inconsistencies in the paper (not about this patient's features): Results say 53 P/LP variants in 42 patients plus 7 VUS in 7 patients, while the Discussion says 57.5% (46/80) carried P/LP variants; Figure 2 legend says 45 children while the text says 46 patients with genetic results.
